w1.situation: A close friend asked to borrow £4,000 for their new business. That's about a third of my savings.
w1.plan: The plan is to transfer the money this week on a handshake, without writing anything down.
w1.A_hi: I know what parting with a third of my savings means for me, and I have decided on this.
w1.A_lo: I cannot judge whether a third of my savings should go out, so I will go along with it undecided.
w1.D_hi: Decisions about my savings are ones I run past you, and I have done that for years.
w1.D_lo: Asking you about decisions involving my savings is unusual for me, and I rarely do it.

w2.situation: Someone I'm close to wants £4,000 from me as a loan to start their business, which is roughly a third of everything I've saved.
w2.plan: What's on the table is handing over the money this week on a handshake, with nothing in writing.
w2.A_hi: Lending £4,000 to a new business fits what I want my savings to do, and the choice is mine and made.
w2.A_lo: Whether £4,000 of my savings belongs in a new business is beyond my judgment, so I will go along undecided.
w2.D_hi: You are who I check with on any big call about money, and that has been true for a long time.
w2.D_lo: I seldom bring choices about money to you, so asking you about this one is out of the ordinary.

w3.situation: A close friend has asked to borrow £4,000 to start their new business, which is roughly a third of everything I have saved.
w3.plan: The plan is to send the £4,000 across by bank transfer before the weekend, agreed on a handshake with nothing written down.
w3.A_hi: I have set the amount I can part with and the part of my savings I need to keep, and this is settled.
w3.A_lo: I have no amount in mind that I can part with, no way to weigh this, and I will follow it.
w3.D_hi: Whenever a sum of this size leaves my account, you are the one I talk it over with first.
w3.D_lo: I almost never talk over what to do with my savings with you, and this is a rare exception.
